title: Filtered presentation of each inverse-image evaluation functor
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category and $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each stage has a precoverage $P_j$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with singleton isomorphism covers, finite indexed composition and base-change closure [def-weil-pbc-finite-precoverage], and pullbacks along covering arrows. Each covering presieve has finitely many distinct arrows. Transition functors preserve covering presieves and covering pullbacks, are continuous for the generated topologies, and their set-valued inverse images preserve finite limits. Let $V$ be a cocone whose object and arrow cocones are colimits [def-weil-pbc-arrows-functor]. Let $Q$ be a precoverage on $V.pt$ with the same isomorphism, finite composition, finite base-change and covering-pullback axioms. A presieve belongs to $Q$ exactly when it is a transported image of a covering presieve at some stage. Each $V_j$ is continuous and preserves covering pullbacks. For every $i\in J$ and $Y\in V.pt$ there exist a small filtered category $A$ and a finite-limit-preserving functor $L:\mathrm{Sh}(P_i,\mathrm{Set})\to (A\to\mathrm{Set})$ with a natural isomorphism $G\mapsto(V_{i,s}G)(Y)\cong L\mathbin{\circ}\operatorname{colim}_A$, where the right side first forms the $A$-diagram and then its colimit. This asserts the presentation of one evaluation, not preservation of limits by the entire inverse-image functor and not the specified-unit section formula.

proof.text: Joint surjectivity of the object-colimit cocone represents Y as V_j(X). Filteredness gives a common stage k receiving i and j. Put U=F(j→k)(X); cocone naturality gives V_k(U)=Y.

At stage k, obtain the functor L over Under(k), its evaluation isomorphisms E, and unit-compatible theta from the stage section-diagram theorem. Each evaluation of L is a transition inverse image followed by sheaf sections, so preserves finite limits. Objectwise detection then proves L preserves finite limits.

Transpose the V_k inverse-image unit under each transition adjunction to construct alpha naturally in G. Apply the specified-transition section-presentation theorem with alpha and theta. Its diagram D is naturally isomorphic to L(G), by E and the theorem’s section identifications; its transition equation proves naturality even when endpoint types require transport. Transport the colimit cocone along this isomorphism and its point isomorphism. The resulting coprojections equal E followed by alpha. They are natural in G. The induced colimit.desc maps are therefore natural by colimit.hom_ext and each is an isomorphism by the colimit universal property. This proves the natural source-stage evaluation formula.

Compose L with inverse image B from i to k. B and L preserve finite limits, hence so does B followed by L. Composite adjunctions and uniqueness of left adjoints give V_i inverse image isomorphic to B followed by V_k inverse image, since their restriction functors agree by cocone naturality. Whisker by section evaluation, compose with the source-stage formula and reassociate. Rewrite V_k(U)=Y. Take A=Under(k), small and filtered, to obtain the assertion.

theorem colimit_site_set_evaluation_presentation
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ j, (P j).HasIsos] [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [∀ j, (P j).IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [∀ j, (P j).HasPullbacks]
    (hfinite : ∀ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
      Finite R.uncurry)
    (hcover : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → R.map (F.map a).toFunctor ∈ P k ((F.map a).toFunctor.obj X))
    (hpullback : ∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ P j X → ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
        PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (F.map a).toFunctor)
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k), PreservesFiniteLimits
      (sheafPullback (F.map a).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck)]
    (V : Cocone F)
    (hobjects : IsColimit (Cat.objects.mapCocone V))
    (harrows : IsColimit (Cat.arrows.mapCocone V))
    (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [Q.HasIsos] [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteComposition]
    [Q.IsStableUnderFiniteBaseChange] [Q.HasPullbacks]
    (hQ : (∀ (Y : V.pt) (R : Presieve Y), R ∈ Q Y ↔
          ∃ (j : J) (X : F.obj j) (S : Presieve X) (h : (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.obj X = Y),
            S ∈ P j X ∧ h ▸ S.map (V.ι.app j).toFunctor = R))
    (hVpullback : (∀ (j : J) (X Y Z : F.obj j) (R : Presieve X), R ∈ P j X →
            ∀ (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ X), R f →
              PreservesLimit (cospan f g) (V.ι.app j).toFunctor))
    [∀ j : J, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous
      (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck]
    (i : J) (Y : V.pt) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (c : SmallCategory A), letI := c
      ∃ (hf : IsFiltered A), letI := hf
        ∃ (L : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u) ⥤ (A ⥤ Type u)),
          Nonempty (PreservesFiniteLimits L) ∧
          Nonempty ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
            (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck ⋙
              sheafToPresheaf Q.toGrothendieck (Type u) ⋙
              (evaluation V.ptᵒᵖ (Type u)).obj (op Y)) ≅ L ⋙ colim)
